title: Journal: 2026-08-25 later, Stage B built and run.sh became the thing you run
body:
One dated entry appended to `docs/JOURNAL.md`. No code.

The morning's entry stopped before most of the day. This covers the rest: Stage B slices 1-3 (#197, #199, #200) and `run.sh` running the whole pipeline (#204), against the design change the owner landed the same day (#203).

**What it records beyond the merge list:**

- **Stage B is three-quarters built and has spent nothing.** One line each for what the three slices actually guarantee, in the form that matters — an unknown field is a fault rather than something to drop; model output hits disk verbatim before it is parsed; three meter readings, the part-way one being what makes it a guard rather than a receipt.
- **The first slices where the implementation was not mine.** Both halves written blind. Two assembled with zero disagreements; slice 2 took 36 failures from one cause, which is now a known defect in how plans are written: a Signatures block names public functions and says nothing about the seam, so two agents invent the boundary twice.
- **Twice today mutation testing caught a test that was checking nothing** — a fixture listing boards in ascending order so a sorted-store mutation looked identical, and "batch 7 is still pending" passing vacuously because the meter's label is `Weekly (7-day)`. Worth recording because it is the argument for the practice: not the defects found in the code, but the tests found to be theatre.
- **Why R7 changed**, in the owner's terms rather than the diff's: a gate that must be passed every few minutes gets propped open; a knob bounded by a real meter reading does not.
- **The model mistake**, plainly. The plan filed a settled question as open because the planner did not check §6, and it had been restated in four places, which is why fixing one never finished it.

**Trimmed to fit, again.** 50 added lines against the 50-line cap. `docs/JOURNAL.md` is not on the `plan` check's uncapped path list, so the file `AGENTS.md` calls the hand-off record is held to the same cap as a typo fix. Nothing was cut that changes a fact — the trimming was prose. Whether the journal belongs on that list beside `docs/architecture.md` and `docs/runs/` is a question for the owner; raising the cap to fit would be gate tampering.

Ran locally: `plan-resolve.sh`, `escape-refs.sh`.
